## Haldoneir

House Haldoneir was a very haughty and old human noble house of Cormyr that was renowned for its historical involvement in the nation's warfare.

Organization
Members of the Haldoneir family tended to be tall and gracile people of striking beauty. They were hardy and long-lived folk who traded in warfare, and because of the battlefield loses, humble in numbers. Many speculated that the family's good and slender looks was the evidence of the Haldoneirs being more than friendly with elves in the past.

The family's heraldry was an image of a dragon's head of a crocodile like maw. The dragon species was not known nor identifiable from the image. The dragon's head silhouette was black and faced left with its maw open, forked tongue extended, and breathing a jet of flames out. The image ended in a straight line that severed the head, three drops of black blood dripping from it as well as a sword that pointed horizontally to the left. The sword was known as the Wyrmdeath.

Activities
Haldoneirs were historic members of Cormyr's Purple Dragons and occasionally, reached high rank and gained trust of the Crown. At least three Haldoneirs reached the rank of Highknights – personal agents of the crown. Many generations of Haldoneirs joined the Purple Dragons, however, the numbers of serving family members greatly reduced with generations, leaving the 14 and 15 century DR Haldoneirs living a live of leisure, financed by the coin from their many properties in Suzail, Selgaunt, and Urmlaspyr.

Base of Operations
The family retained Wyrmdown, a large countryside manse northeast of Immersea. Another family holding was Ormvraezel Keep, a castle with its own hunting forest and farmlands, in northwestern Sembia. The hunting lodge called the Boarhunt Towers was located in central Sembia. And the main home for the family was located in Suzail – High Oronel, as well as several secret townhouses in the capital and two apartments in Marsember.

Relationships
Opposed to the Crown of Cormyr, Haldoneirs allied themselves with shady Sembian organizations such as Fire Knives and various slaver organizations. The family was not above using Fire Knives to dispose of its relatives and selling their own daughters into slavery when coin was sparse.

History
The family's first notable individual was Ryneth Haldoneir who lived during the reign of Ondeth Obarskyr. Ryneth was a farmer, archer, and an occasional mercenary who resided in the settlement that would eventually become Suzail. The Haldoneir family arrived to Cormyr from elsewhere and remained part of the Forest Kingdom for many centuries to follow. Despite that, the family was never known as the Dragon Throne loyalists. By the late 14 and 15 centuries DR, Haldoneirs were commonly known as one of the "founding families" of Cormyr and having "blood as regal as any family of the realm." In the early days of the Forest Kingdom, Haldoneirs took arms on behalf of the early Obarskyr monarches. Tales also claimed that the family was known for taming dragons in the years past, however, that was nothing but a legend, inspired by imaginative minstrels and the family's sets of scale armor and dragon's head helmets and other dragon-like adornments.

Haldoneirs owed their ennoblement to widow Lady Vaerestra Haldoneir, who loyally served as an advisor to King Dhalmass Obarskyr and was highly regarded by the High Wizard Jorunhast. She shielded King Dhalmas from a poisoned dagger with her own body, sacrificing her life in the process. Thankful for the deed, the monarch made the family into a noble house and gave Mreldon Haldoneir, Vaerestra soldier son, the title of the first Lord Haldoneir.

However, by the early part of the reign of Rhigaerd Obarskyr II, Haldoneirs became embittered over Lord Esmarl Haldoneir's removal as the Royal Privy Advisor due to him becoming corrupt and concealing his investigation's from the Crown in exchange for bribes. Since Esmarl's fall from grace, the Haldoneirs became some of the most avid proponents of such claims as Obarskyrs not being true rulers of Cormyr, and that they were nothing but old-blood family that took the throne through lies and immoral actions. In the 14 century DR, the family's attitude towards the crown was well known through royal spies and Vangerdahast Aeiulvana, the Royal Magician. As such, House Haldoneir was cut off from the King's Court and the family was largely ignored. The only reason, according to truthful rumors, why the family had not been stripped of their nobility was due to at least two Haldoneir ladies begging King Azoun not to disgrace their family. One of them was Lady Aglathna Haldoneir of whom king was very found of. Her successor, Lady Ulandra Haldoneir, was also instrumental as she became a close friend of King Azoun's. Despite his affections, King Azoun also had Vangerdahast enspell his loins so none of his proclivities with Ladies Haldoneir resulted in an Obarskyr bastard.

By the late 15 century DR, the Haldoneir Family were stagnant, enjoying lives of luxury and hedonism. They lived off the real estate coin and spent it on mistresses and brightlads, participated in many voguish cults, conspiracies, and business fads that failed and went our of fashion more often than not. They were also known for sponsoring merchants and cabals who sought to evade the crown's rule and groups that fostered seditious intents. The Haldoneir numbers were also kept in check thanks to common feuds among themselves, resulting in assassinations.

Members
Asmrella Haldoneir, a young daughter of the Sembian Haldoneir family who, alongside Dorlarra, Feaenrelle, Paerelle, and nieces Borlatha and Daunameire, who disappeared in early 1369 DR, sold into slavery.
Amandras Haldoneir, a Highknight of the Purple Dragons, serving King Galaghard Obarskyr III.
Baerlon Haldoneir, a Highknight of the Purple Dragons, serving King Proster Obarskyr.
Daeromur Haldoneir, the family's sadistic patriarch in the late 14 century DR, and a hedonistic aeravair of alcohol.
Eldaun Haldoneir, "the hidden Haldoneir" who disappeared in a fire as a baby, secretly entrusted by his mother, Taerenthe, to be raised in Westgate, away from House Haldoneir.
Galard Haldoneir, a Highknight of the Purple Dragons, serving King Palaghard Obarskyr I.
Flaernd Haldoneir, a bookish family member from Sembia who was murdered alongside his two uncles, Baerand and Thruleon, by the Fire Knives on Haldoneirs's behest in the late 14 century DR.
Marluke Haldoneir, a heir of the family who was tortured and murdered by other Haldoneirs in the summer of 1367 DR as a punishment for gambling away many of the Haldoneir assets in Sembia.
Raskrel Haldoneir, lazy and spineless man, allegedly, Daeromur's only surviving son as of the late 14 century DR.
Taerenthe Haldoneir, a youth and beauty obsessed wife of Daeromur.

## Hallucinations

Hallucinations were perceived aspects of reality that did not actually exist. These delusions could take any form and have any level of detail, and were able to be induced with illusion magic.

Acquisition
Most illusion spells created false aspects of reality perceived by all, such as hallucinatory forest and hallucinatory terrain. Some insidious spells directly affected the senses of specific people, leaving others unaware of what was happening. These personal magical hallucinations were typically phantasms.

 Mental prison created a powerful and terrifying internal illusion that could kill the victim with its own perception of danger.
 Phantasmal force and phantasmal killer created an elaborate and believable internal illusion that the victim could be harmed by.

Effects

When hallucinating, a person was witness to sights, sounds, smells, and tactile sensations that did not align with reality. These could be as simple as ordinary objects, as personal as disembodied voices that gave advice or instructions, or as complex as entire people that could be interacted with. They were especially likely to strike during moments of stress like combat, making it exceptionally dangerous for them.

Notable Affected
 Hagen Silverthumb dissociated and hallucinated a friend after escaping from Egil Hakon.

Lord Harkon was one of the high-ranked members of Halaster Blackcloak's nameless conspiracy revealed in the  by the Seven Sisters. During the meeting, he suggested this connection gave them the opportunity to set an ambush for the Simbul, who'd come for Thaltar Glaervar. Thaltar then revealed he'd been attacked by her earlier that day, but had already slain her; he revealed a wand he'd taken from her body. The wand turned out to be the Simbul in spell-shape, who immediately set about the task of slaying them all.

He was the last one slain by the Simbul's spell-sphere shape after he employed a prismatic wall shaped into a sword to strike at the sphere. However, the sphere turned into a snake, the snake went down his throat, and made him explode.

## Hafkris

Hafkris was a half-orc fighter who operated as a slaver onboard the ill-fated pirate galley sailing towards Westhaven that crashed into the coast of the Island of Viledel in the early 14 century DR.

History
Hafkris believed his captain mad for sailing during storm season, which resulted in the deaths of all the crew except the captain, Hafkris, and a large portion of the slave cargo. During the storm, Hafkris threw the captain overboard and would later have no regrets.

After the crash, Hafkris got drunk and wandered the beach in a stupor, marching up and down the front of the galley singing grotesque sailor-songs. Unbeknownst to him, the remaining slaves managed to free themselves. He planned to retrieve his heavy crossbow and 50 quarrels, and secure the slaves. His fate is unknown.

Personality
Before the crash, Hafkris took pleasure in taunting the slaves with their destination of Westhaven, a place he described as "the greatest pirate city in the world". If a slave mouthed off to him, he would take his belt off and hit them repeatedly with it.

After the crash, he was one step close to going crazy himself. He did not regret murdering the captain, only that he did so too late to save the ship. He even blamed the galley for "failing him". Despite his many failings, if he was to be overwhelmed by the slaves, he would surrender, but only to bide his time to escape and either chain them or slay them.

Abilities
He was proficient in sword, dagger, crossbow and pike.

Possessions
He wore studded leather and carried a broadsword and dagger, and left his heavy crossbow in the aft of the galley after the crash. His gear was valued at 53 gp.

## Halaster's quaff

Halaster's quaff was a potion designed to "Master Death", created by "He Who is to be Feared: Halaster". The quaff was an immensely dangerous potion that could render the imbiber immune to death magic and numerous other boons, but it also had a high chance of granting death.

Description
When the elixir was successfully completed, it had a pitch-black color and viscosity of syrup. It tasted like bone marrow, the flavor that Elminster Aumar considered distasteful.

Powers
Once Halaster's quaff was consumed, the imbiber immediately suffered physical damage from the drink, and one of the several outcomes occurred, depending on pure luck: 1) instant death, 2) even further physical damage, 3) feeblemindedness, 4) one of the limbs withered to the bone, 5) the skin turned chalk-shite and eyes turned red gaining permanent infravision, 6) gender and sex changed, 7) loss of powers and adventuring experience while gaining physical vitality, 8) gained immunity to chill touch and energy drain in all forms, 9) all positive effects of the elixir were gained but faded away after two-to-sixteen months, and lastly, 10) Halaster's quaff was fully successful. Halaster's quaff could be consumed as many times as one could procure it or create it, and its consecutive consumptions did not change the chances of receiving one result or the other.

A successful imbibing of Halaster's quaff gave the luck individual permanent immunity to chill touch, strength, energy, or ability being drained, paralysis, feeblemindedness, disintegration, and death magics. They received a boost to their vitality, and, every time they stood at death's door, they received the benefits of free action and haste. They also could not age via the used of the haste. Lastly, instead of falling unconscious or dying from sustained damage, the imbiber was transported to the Ethereal plane, floating there in stasis, until it was returned to the Prime Material plane via magic, help from others, or similar means. If the body sustained enough damage whilst in the Etheral plane, they, nevertheless, perished.

Creation
Firstly, Halaster's quaff had to be mixed in a vessel made of ivory or bone and stirred with a bone spoon. Its ingredients included powdered bone of an undead skeleton, ghoul tongue flesh, at least six drops of blood squeezed from the heart of a peryton, mimic flesh, zombie eyeball, at least three scaled from a snake that made a human skull its lair, powdered shell of a dragon's or wyvern's egg, and a potion of sweet water. Once the ingredients were stirred, the light spell had to be cast onto the mixture, and the potion had to be consumed before the light magic expired.

History
The formula for Halaster's quaff was engraved into the floor of a certain chamber in the depths of Undermountain, the mega-dungeon underneath the City of Splendors, Waterdeep, and signed as being created by "He Who is to be Feared: Halaster." The relative ease of coming across the recipe, it being copied, and brought to the surface by numeours adventurers, made Halaster's quaff famous, often used, despite its deadliness. Many adventurers who produced the quaff and consumed it found themselves dead, maimed, or damaged. Those who left crippled by the concoction often attempted repeated imbibing in hopes of achieving the potion's sucesesfull effects of curing the potion-inflicted afflictions.

It was known that Halaster Blackcloak consumed this potion, and at least one of his apprentices stole the formula from their master and carved it into Undermountain chamber's floor. After the formula was shared, it was believed that Halaster improved the recipe and gained the elixir's full benefits. This new formula, however, was never recorded or found, and its existence was only known thanks to a single brave adventurer who asked the Mad Mage about it and received an answer.

## Harbaldur

Harbaldur was believed to be one of the first inhabitants of the town of Loklee, long before it would be known by other names. Harbaldur became well-known for his work forging grand, sturdy, yet ornamental castle and vault gates. As the dwarf traded and did business, the locals gave him a nickname – Baldur. With time, his business partners and new acquaintances began to believe that Baldur was his full name. Some historians believed that the name "Baldur" was adopted by the locals who began referring to the village of Gray Harbor as Baldur's Gate sometime before the .

Centuries later, Harbaldur's name was overshadowed by the adventurer and investor Balduran, who became known as the founder of Baldur's Gate after returning from a profitable expedition and investing heavily in his hometown sometime in the mid-1000s DR.

Thegglis' brother Thegglis was a fellow caravan guard, and the youngest siblings Hemjax, Maggie, and others, still lived with Oliver and Kroyce as of the late 15 century DR.

History
In the, as the Cult of the Absolute threatened Baldur's Gate's safety, two of the Tetoco children, Blunce and Harvel, applied to join the Flaming Fist Company. According to the letter signed by Manip Seyama of the Basilisk Gate barracks, both men, Blunce and Harvel, were approved and commanded to immediately report to the Seatower of Balduran to receive gear and equipment training.

## Hall of the Raven

The Hall of the Raven, also known as Raven Hall, was a massive keep in Ravens Bluff and the stately home of the city's Knights Council.

Location
The Hall of the Raven stood on the corner of Raphiel Road & Raven Way, in the Altarside neighborhood of Ravens Bluff's Temple District.

Structure
This keep was an imposing structure, standing five stories tall and noted for its arched windows.

Activities
The Knights Council conducted all knightly title ceremonies within the Hall of the Raven. Following the destruction of the Ravens Bluff Hall of Records in 1371 DR, the keep was also used as an archive for the records of all knightly orders.

History
On a late night in the, a large fire broke out in the Ravens Bluff Hall of Records. The building was completely destroyed by the blaze before the Red Ravens could control it, burning many records of the city's knightly orders. Not all of these records were completely lost, as many had copies stored within the Raven Museum in case of just such a blaze. The Knights Council had a swift and pronounced response to the incident, promptly printing fliers requesting all knights in the city to notify the Council of their allegiances by providing copies of their official heraldry, the names of their sponsors (the knights who wrote their letters of recommendation), and any awards and knightly honors they own.

In the wake of this, it came to light that there were many bogus knights in Ravens Bluff with no proper claim to their title, a criminal offense under Ravenian law. These knight impersonators, a majority of whom were adventurers, had their titles stripped away. Additionally, the Knights Council made a staunch vow that from then on the records for all knightly orders were going to be safely kept within the Hall of the Raven, even if the Hall of Records was rebuilt.

Havilyn lived with two other men who handled abundant money but were not known to practice any trade, more likely to be investors than merchants. History
In, local Hastarl thieves Eladar and Farl hurled local coin-lass, Shandathe, into the bedchambers of the baker Hannibur through the second-story window to keep her safe from the forces of a local dandy that had purchased her services and then been thwarted. They took brief notice that he slept in women's lingerie. Afterwards, to their surprise, there had been no word of what happened after Shandathe woke up. Shandathe made it a point to return to his home on at least some nights, which they eavesdropped on at least once. They got married just about the same day on which the thief Eladar the Dark (actually Elminster) was going to leave Hastarl; he paid them a visit, and dropped gold coins between the two of them as they slept.

In, the armsmen of King Belaur Aumar broke into his home to pull out his wife, Shandathe, to whom the king had seen and taken a fancy. They also knocked him out. During the siege that followed the arrival of the prince Elminster Aumar, come at the head of a force bent on ending the reign of Belaur and his Magelords of Athalantar, Hannibur snuck in through the tumult and managed to stab the Mage Royal Undarl Dragonrider from behind. After the prince slew King Belaur, and fainted, Hannibur picked up the Sword of the Stag, and used it to hold at bay the King's courtiers who meant to assassinate the prince, until the sorceress Myrjala Talithyn arrived at the throne room with his wife, Shandathe, and aided the prince.

## Harrowfast

Harrowfast was a dwarven stronghold in the Cambro Mountains on Gwynneth in the Moonshae Isles, although it had been abandoned by the dwarves as of the late 15 century DR.

Location
It sat in a mountain on the northern edge of the valley of Synnoria. When approaching from outside Synnoria, it was accessed through a narrow ravine on the mountain's eastern slope, marked by black stone covered in reliefs of ancient deities and rulers. To reach the stronghold from Synnoria required a steep ascent through the Synnorian fog beginning in the woods on the northern border. This path first involved climbing through vines and rhododendron trees, then scaling a cascade of boulders before finally reaching a set of crumbing, moss-covered steps of shoddy construction.

Structure
The main, eastern entrance was a massive stone gateway that descended down into the dwarf-cut passages and rooms within the mountain.

The Synnorian entrance arrived via a narrow gate onto a stone piazza exposed to the elements on the southern side of the mountain, which featured giant stone columns and statues from which alabaster lanterns hung from iron chains. The entrance to Harrowfast was a set of descending stairs leading into the mountain and to a cloakroom with a washbasin. Opposite this entrance, the courtyard connected via a narrow causeway to a lookout point atop a pinnacle of rock above the fog-shrouded valley of Synnoria.

Interior
New arrivals entered into a stone agora large enough to host small armies. From here, stone staircases descended further. One of these staircases (through a gate which was carved to look like a demon's open mouth) led to a bathhouse.

Down the steps from the exit to the southward lookout point and passed a double row of marble columns, there was a nearly circular council chamber hewn from the rock. It was shaped as a deep amphitheater with tiered, semicircular benches rising up the western wall. In the circular bottom of the chamber, atop a dais, sat a  stone meeting table surrounded by heavy chairs. This table was smooth marble on top but the underside was adorned with carvings of constellations, phases of the moon, and an image of the sun featuring a face with wide eyes. The whole room was lit by natural shafts leading to the outside, which also served to provide ventilation, but was dim and damp.

A great hall near the council chamber was used to host large banquets and meals. Elsewhere, marble sepulchers had been used to lay to rest slain warriors. Deeper still were guardhouses and a multitude of caves and mines extending all the way into the Underdark. The forgotten "guts" of the fortress contained a multiude of rusted clockwork machinery.

Defenses
Harrowfast was well-fortified. The council chambers included a secret trap for hasty escapes: the dais could be made to spin down a corkscrew track on iron wheels to bring anyone at the table into the depths of Harrowfast, from where the Underdark was readily accessible. Activating this escape route required closing the eyelids of the face in the sun on the table's underside, which triggered the clockwork mechanism.

History
The dwarves fled from Harrowfast in the late 14 century DR.The Rose of Sarifal does not clarify exactly when or why the dwarves abandoned Harrowfast, but the implication is that they fled to escape the expulsion of non-fey from Gwynneth by the leShay. As of the late 15 century DR, Harrowfast was used as an outpost by the Llewyrr elves of the Knights of Synnoria. In particular, it was used as a staging ground for Lords Askepel and Mindarion to plot the overthrow of their rulers, the leShay of Sarifal. These elves stocked the bathhouse with woven mats, pillows, quilts, and wine, and had their Ffolk slaves maintain the enclave, play music, and keep its lanterns lit.

Harrowfast was discovered to lie close to a tunnel exit dug by fomorians and their slaves that extended through the Underdark to their lands in the north, which proved fortuitous in the late 1470s DR when the elves and the fomorians discussed the possibility of an alliance against the leShay. Negotiations began after a fomorian princess, Marabaldia, was rescued from the leShay by a group of human rebels known as the Winterglen Claw. The humans, elves, and fomorians made grand overtures of working together, but these were quickly found to be hollow. Although they had amassed a combined army estimated at 10,000 strong, the three sides could not agree on what Sarifal's future should look like. This came to a head after Rurik, captain of the Winterglen Claw, and Suka, a friend of Marabaldia, were attacked by a wyvern on the lookout point, forcing them to flee into Synnoria. This accidental trespass was enough to offend the Llewyrr who guarded the valley, who attempted to imprison them. The pair slew the guards and fled, forcing a violent end to the nascent alliance.

## Harbinger Kin

Harbinger Kin was a variety of enchanted great swords created on the Sword Coast North in the late 14 century DR, with the original and the most powerful variety being the artifact that once was sought after by Kwukgixrin, an illithid brain.

Powers
There existed three variants of the Harbinger Kin, each possessed a +1, +3, and +8 enchantments what made the sword's edge deadlier and guided the wielder's hand towards the target. All three versions were powered by magical flames that burned the target upon a successful slash.

A Harbinger Kin could be created from an enchanted great sword and a slab of adamantite.

History
The original Harbinger Kin was an artifact that belonged to a powerful adventurer who delved into the dangers of the Underdark sometime before the late 14 century DR. When the adventurer fell victim to Kwukgixrin and his mind was consumed, the elder brain became obsessed with finding the artifact sword. It sent out its mind flayers to scour the Underdark in search of the greatsword that was hidden be the adventurer before his death. However, adventurer's twin brother recovered Harbinger Kin before Kwukgixrin's thralls were able to find it. The twin was strong in his own right and slaughtered the elder brain's thralls and its illithids before leaving the Underdark.

More common versions of Harbinger Kin with a simpler +1 enchantment were forged by Master Blacksmith Marrok of Shining Knight Arms and Armor shop of Neverwinter to help the heroes who sought the cure from the dreaded Wailing Death of the . Later the same year, more powerful versions were created by Master Blacksmith Barun of Beorunna's Well to help the forces of Neverwinter stand against Lady Aribeth the Betrayer, who led a marching army of Luskan in the deadly but short-lived Neverwinter-Luskan war.

## Hastarl

Hastarl was the capital city of Athalantar in the 2 to 4 centuries DR. Secomber was later built upon its ruins.

Description
Like most cities, Hastarl was crowded and dirty, as the city was dense rather than sprawling.

The northern side of the city held a number of rich houses, with spired towers.

There was an old burial ground across the city from the Kissing Wench festhall; it was walled, had trees planted, and had already grown dilapidated by .

Side streets to the right of one of the ports held residences without walls, where well-off but not wealthy people lived

Geography
Geographical Features
Hastarl was built on the crossing of the Delimbiyr River and the Unicorn Run.

Demographics
The population was about 17,000 people in the early-to-mid 3 century DR, reaching 26,000 at its peak.

Government
Hastarl was the capital of Athalantar.

Trade
During the reign of Belaur Aumar, the Magelords of Athalantar did not allow guilds in the city.

Sometimes, traders of Calishite silks whose stocks hadn't run dry closer to the sea made the trip to Hastarl to trade.

Defenses
Hastarl was a walled city.

History
Hastarl was destroyed in, by an orcish horde.

The ruins were reclaimed by the founding of Secomber in the .

Notable Locations
The Kissing Wench, a festhall
Ansildabar's Last Rest
The mage Orthalar owned a house in the city.
The baker Hannibur had a bakery. There were silver-bit baths nearby.
The trader Havilyn had a home, with sewers fed by and discharging into the Unicorn Run, close to the docks; the location was in the same zone as the upscale houses.
The trader Fentarn had a home, too.
The trader Nalith owned at least one warehouse.
There were shrines to Sune, Helm, Lathander, Tyche, and Tyr. There was also a temple of Mystra, in disuse during the reign of King Belaur.
Upriver past the wall (almost certainly the north wall, upstream along the Unicorn Run) there was a refuse pit around which traders often camped.
West of the city, outside the wall, there was a nameless shrine of Mystra on a grave-knoll, surrounded by a low wall.

## Harper Lodge

The Harper Lodge was a hidden Harper base in the King's Forest of Cormyr used in the 15 century DR.

Location
The lodge was within the King's Forest, and best accessed by following along Greenweald Lane from the northern edge before going off the road and traveling through the woods for a time.

Description
The lodge was a two-story structure with several outbuildings, a small grain field, and a vineyard. The interior was largely a single chamber that served as a meeting and dining area, with the second floor as a mezzanine around it. A basement level was used as a wine cellar and secure repository.

History
Following the Shadovar invasion of Wheloon in the mid-1480s DR, the Harpers raced to track down the Abyssal Planus Mechanus Nether Scroll that Oriphaun Huntsilver had stolen from the Shadovar and scattered in pieces along the High Road. One such piece was found by Bensen Virandson, who noted that the artifact was radiating an aura of energy that made it extremely easy to track, and so needed to be carefully contained and hidden with a special strongbox found at the Harper Lodge. He was joined by reinforcements sent by Rina Belostos from Eveningstar, who escorted him along Greenweald Lane as they fought through the Netherese wizards and their hired mercenaries, including the elite forces of Dom. The lodge was eventually found by enemy forces thanks to the woodsy wisdom of the druid Rand, letting Dom and Slam beat Bensen there, and causing a short battle in the basement as both sides struggled for the Nether Scroll piece, ending in the Harpers' favor.

## Hand of the mage

A hand of the mage was an enchanted amulet that, aptly named in both appearance and use, allowed its wearer to call upon a mage hand spell at their leisure.

Description
It was nothing less than a mummified elven hand, typically attached as a pendant to a gold chain and worn around the neck as though it was any other amulet. Altogether, it weighed about . Anyone who sought to create their own hand of the mage could alternatively used the right hand of a mephit as a power component.

Powers
An experienced-enough artisan of magical items needed only be able to cast the mage hand spell themselves to imbue it into their hand of the mage, which could then be activated by the wielder's will. They could do so as often as they wished, being restricted only by the spell's own limitations.

Notable Owners
By Faerûn's late 14 century DR, a hand of the mage was a typical piece of equipment used by experienced Red Wizards of Thay, as well as by Chondathans as a whole. So pervasive was the use of such hands among the latter that, in any sufficiently populous city of the Vilhon Reach, Sembia, the Dragon Coast, and Cormyr, the item was normally discounted a tenth of its typical cost whenever sold.

Specific individuals who owned a hand of the mage included:
 Dark Stag, an ex-adventuress and the local Herald of Silverymoon.
 Helcav, a drow wizard faithful to Laveth, whose mummified hand of the mage was specifically that of a drow.
 The green dragon Claugiyliamatar, as well as the dracolich Daurgothoth, both of whom kept a hand among their hoards.

Hands of the mage could also be found on the distant world of Oerth, and even on that of Krynn, typically in the varied pouches of the kender.

 Gauntlets of the mage hand, which, though they served a similar purpose, were worn on the wielder's own hands rather than around their neck.

## Hadarai El'or'riandir

Hadarai El’or’riandi was a male eladrin minor lord residing on the island of Gwynneth in the Moonshae Isles as of the late 15 century DR.

Personality
He was generous and gracious to his friends and to the friends of his friends.

While he appreciated other cultures, he was fully convinced of the superiority of his high elven culture over all others.

Activities
He was a dealer of elven magic items, notably magic weapons, magic armors (such as eladrin armor), and accessories (such as elven cloaks).

Lord Hadarai was one of a small number of Sarifal eladrin who opposed the isolationist policies of High Lady Ordalf, and in defiance of them, he had traveled among the other Moonshae Isles, befriended and sought humans, and even invited some of these friends for clandestine meetings on Gwynneth's shores. He was known to arrange such meetings at a ruined temple of Chauntea in the Winterglen forest about a half mile (1 kilometer) from the coast of the Strait of Oman.

Relationships
One of his trusted vassals was an eladrin spellcaster named Randall, whom he would send on missions to far off lands.

Haradai had forged a strong friendship with the human Daffyd Mac Lyrr during his travels.

He was generally mistrusting of drow and tieflings.

History
Hadarai's travels took him to the island of Alaron and to the town of Warlsby in particular on multiple occasions, where he became acquainted with the ruling Mac Lyrr family.

By the late 15 century DR, Hadarai sought to establish trade with the Isles beyond Gwynneth, seeking to sell elven jewelry and magic items in exchange for foreign books, lore, magic, and other goods. However, trade with foreign realms was forbidden by the laws of Sarifal. Hadarai did not wish to break these laws, but he believed that as long as he only did business with foreign elves, his business ventures would technically be legitimate.

In the, he arranged for a clandestine meeting with Daffyd on Gwynneth to discuss establishing trade between their realms.

Sometime later, he sent his servant Randall to aid the Feywild town of Baeladar Yaaira in the Cloakwood, which was threatened by fomorians. He instructed Randall to offer rewards for information about portals to and from the Feywild.

## Harakhti Uprisings

The Harakhti Uprisings were a great slave rebellion of the Shoon Imperium in the early 3 century DR.

History
On the Feast of the Moon in 204 DR, the gladiator-slave Harakhti broke from a small fighting arena in Almraiven and assembled an army of thousands of slaves and poor freemen who sought to fight the Shoon Imperium. Leading them north, he amassed more than 25,000 people from the Almraiven Peninsula. Though they were mostly an untrained mob, they were filled with an unquenchable lust for freedom and were fortified by many skilled gladiatorial slaves. They broke through the Shoon garrisons to the north and escaped into the Land of the Lions, gathering more followers as they went, and soon had 120,000 people—the largest single army in the region.

The newly-crowned Qysar Amahl Shoon VI responded in person at the head of his own army in late Uktar of the, eager to prove that the Shoon were not afraid to get their hands dirty. In the only notable achievement of his short reign, Amahl used his military experience to deftly meet the slave army in battle north and west of Ankhapur. After their forces had mutually destroyed each other by inflicting a total of 180,000 casualties, he then engaged in a fierce duel with Harakhti. Though the Emperor won, Harakhti considered it a kind of victory to force the Emperor of Shoon to fight a slave, and Amahl was forced to admit that although he was a mad dog and was put down like one, Harakhti had been a brilliant fighter. In order to make his point clear, he had the recaptured slaves—over half of all the slaves that had revolted—staked alive along the roadways of the empire, to slowly die in a most public manner. After returning to Shoonach and two days of celebrations, he was then assassinated by his brother, Shoon IV.

Although the slave revolt was ended by the duel and battle, a great many people were freed and disappeared beyond the authority of Shoon by Harakhti's actions. Centuries later, Harakhti the Deliverer was recounted as a heroic figure by the nomadic folk of Arnaden, whose ancestors had been freed by him. Conversely, in Calimshan the Shoon campaign was commemorated in the Sadimmin and Nallojal with the Chains of Harakhti decoration, awarded for service during battle.

## Harper of Legend

Harpers of legend were extraordinary Master Harpers who were graced with powerful divine blessings bestowed by the Seven Gods of the Dancing Place who in ages past had given rise to the Harpers.

Activities
Every such Harper bore a long record of bold deeds and daring exploits. Yet even in death their service often did not cease. Cylyria Dragonbreast and Dathlue Mistwinter, for example, remained vigilant beyond the grave, sometimes serving as mentors to Harpers of their own time and those in training.

Culture
Many Harpers served their organization for long years before achieving legendary status, yet at times the Seven themselves would intervene, bestowing their blessings upon individuals who had never belonged to the Harpers, should they prove a force for good worthy of such divine favor. Yet any such individual would have probably drawn the attention of the Harpers themselves, before the need for divine intervention. In their future, such Harpers would probably have their names spoken in the same breath as those of other great Harpers who have gone before them: Storm Silverhand, Cylyria Dragonbreast, or Arilyn Moonblade. Sometimes even after death, these Harpers participated in the life and culture of their organization, by giving advice or training new and old Harpers.

Abilities
Harpers of legend were always versed in at least two of the following four skills: diplomacy, insight into others, nature knowledge, or stealth.

These heroes were well-traveled individuals that learned more than most people do.

Mightier Harpers of legend bore a special blessing from the goddess Mielikki, allowing them to push their bodies harder than usually possible and thus perform astonishing feats unique to their non-Harper training, and more often.

Even mightier legendary Harpers received a blessing from Tymora, which allowed them to avoid powerful attacks, or stop negative conditions that were possible to avoid, even when they failed at avoiding them.

Once per day, when one of the most powerful Harpers of legend died, their body would disintegrate into silver dust and their spirit would walk free. When this happened, they retained their learned skills and attributes, became insubstantial, could pass through solid objects, were immune to poison, and were more resistant to damaging necrotic energy. After an extended rest, their bodies would restore themselves. If they died in this form, they were finally dead. However, thanks to the blessings of the Seven Gods of the Dancing Place, a Harper of legend was immortal in a sense, able to transcend this "permanent" death and endure as ghost Harpers, their vigilance undimmed.

History
In ages past, when the Harpers were founded, the Seven Gods of the Dancing Place collectively extended their blessings to mortals who vowed to fight against evil in the Year of the Dawn Rose, 720 DR. These blessings were the basis for the abilities of the adventurers called Harpers of legend.

## Harun el Humuz

Harun el Humuz was a stone carver in the city of Calimport, Calimshan, in the late 14 century DR. Together with his brother Nur, he ran the Brothers Humuz business.

Personality
Harun more focused on the trade than his brother.

Activities
Circa 1370 DR, Brothers Harun and Nur specialized in carving murals into stone and mud-brick walls on the insides of fine homes, often enhancing the building's value or social status. The brothers worked well together without issue, but when a client desired to paint over the finished mural, Nur got upset at his artistry being soiled and stormed off. Harun was left to finish the work.

In addition, the Brothers Humuz were spies for the Rundeen mercantile consortium. After working for long periods in wealthy clients' homes, they reported what they saw and heard to their Rundeen masters every sixmonth.

## Harold Butterbisk

Harold Butterbisk was the owner of the Butterbisk Inn in Waterdeep, the City of Splendors, sometime before the late 15 century DR.

History
At some point before the, Harold Butterbisk ran the Butterbisk Inn and used the enchanted heavy crossbow that was named after himself – Harold. The namesake crossbow had an engraving on its stock that read "Quaffing is a shootable offence." At some point after the Butterbisk Inn changed owners, its name was changed.

## Harold

Harold was a unique enchanted heavy crossbow from the mercantile nation of Sembia, created sometime before the late 14 century DR as a commission for Fitzallus the Footpad.

Powers
The original Harold was a heavy crossbow with a simple +2 enchantment that guided the bolts towards their goal and increased its damage potential. Additionally, targets struck with Harold's bolts had a good chance of suffering the effects of the doom spell.

The version of the item from the 15 century DR was known for its +1 enchantment and the ability to inflict bane on its targets.

History
Sometime before the late 14 century DR, Fitzallus the Footpad, a bard of Sembia, commissioned this enchanted crossbow. He endlessly praised the new weapon. The bard's excitement over the crossbow was such that his friends began teasing the bard, saying that the weapon was Fitzallus's new "best friend" and he needed to give it an appropriate name. When the enchanted crossbow was ready, Fitzallus proudly strolled into a tavern with a bright smile and announced to his friends the weapon's name: Harold. Several months later, Fitzallus died during a burglary. According to his will, Harold was to be buried with the bard, yet the crossbow disappeared before the funeral.

Sometime later, by the, Harold ended up in the hands of Rhynwis, the head of a fledgling thieves' guild on the Sword Coast North during Caelar Argent's crusade against Avernus.

Another copy of the weapon, or perhaps the original with its history misattributed, surfaced in the 15 century DR in the City of Splendors, Waterdeep. They said that Harold was named after Harold Butterbisk, the owner of the Butterbisk Inn. That weapon had an engraving on its stock that read: "Quaffing is a shootable offense." That crossbow ended up in the hands of Zarys, the woman who led a Zhentarim cell operating from the caverns underneath Waukeen's Rest in the Chionthar Valley in the .

## Haarl's Treatise on Dragonkind

Haarl's Treatise on Dragonkind was a book of draconic knowledge that contained many hidden secrets of dragons and other draconic creatures, penned by Haarl, sometime before the late 15 century DR.

History
By the 1480s DR, the Cult of the Dragon had been using Haarl's Treatise on Dragonkind, as well as Breyer's Draconic Investigations, to acquire much of the forbidden knowledge hidden in the books' pages. Both books were in the hands of the Cult's leaders when they led a skirmish on the shores of the isle of Tuern. Once the Cult's forces were defeated, both books were retrieved by the forces of Neverwinter.

## Haurugg

Haurugg was a woodsman of the Storm Horns during the late 15 century DR.

Description
Haurugg was a large half-orc fellow with gray skin and a black mohawk and sideburns.

History

Around the time of the Shadovar invasion of Wheloon, the forces of Risen Netheril took over part of the Storm Horns as Archwizard Amskar built his army. Haurugg lived in a cave near Yarrow Glade and wisely tried to avoid any interactions with the growing threat, only for them to take over his home while he was out. He might have been lucky enough to run into Harpers who were working with Oriphaun Huntsilver nearby, and then helped clear out the Netherese invaders.
